core_job: Work out a real-life sum on a ruled sheet. Each line works out as you type: arithmetic, references to other lines (#n, prev), percentages, unit conversions, currency conversions, and a pinned total. Sheets are saved, searchable and shareable. The user is someone who mixes currencies, units and dates and has to keep or hand over the working, such as a freelancer billing abroad, an expat or traveller doing an expense claim, or someone planning a DIY job. The existing 30 tools stop being five tabs of separate destinations. They move into a Tools drawer, and each one except BMI has 'Add to sheet'.
signature: Rate on the day. A currency line can carry a date ('38.50 EUR on 14 Sep in USD'). It is converted at the European Central Bank reference rate for that date, via Frankfurter's keyless historical endpoint. Verified 2026-10-12: 2026-09-14 gives EUR to USD 1.1551; Saturday 2026-10-10 returns the 2026-10-09 rate of 1.1206; 1999-01-04 works; earlier and future dates return 404. The rate and the date actually used are printed under the line. Undated lines are pinned to their first rate, so a saved sheet shows the same answer next month, and re-pricing happens only on an explicit tap. Text and CSV exports list every rate, its date and the ECB source. The App Store descriptions of Soulver 4, CalcMate and Calculator₊ mention only live or latest rates. How those apps actually behave is not verified.

A pure-Dart sheet_engine handles the line grammar (arithmetic through lib_calc, #n/prev, %, unit and currency conversions, total that leaves out lines with other units or currencies). Auto-saved under sheets_v1 in shared_preferences. The Sheets list has search, rename, duplicate, and delete with Undo. No fee, margin or remittance audit, which is NexusTransferPay's lane
